graft.title: WSL gets no AMD-V despite nestedVirtualization=true: no svm, no /dev/kvm in vgwsl2
graft.need: On vghydra (Ryzen 9 7900, Windows 10.0.26200.9711, WSL 2.7.14.0, kernel 6.18.33.2-2), %USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig has [wsl2] nestedVirtualization=true, and the WSL VM has restarted since (uptime 8 s when checked, 2026-10-22). Inside it: `grep -c svm /proc/cpuinfo` is 0, /dev/kvm doesn't exist, and dmesg says `Hyper-V: Nested features: 0x0`. Virtualization-Based Security is running (Win32_DeviceGuard VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus = 2). Needed: whatever on the Windows side makes Hyper-V expose AMD-V to the WSL VM, declared in this repo so it holds on the next machine too (a feature, a setting, or a decision that it can't with VBS / Memory Integrity on, and what the tradeoff is). The Linux side is ready: kvm-amd.ko ships in WSL's /lib/modules, Nix's system-features include kvm and nixos-test, and the user is in the kvm group (vg-dotfiles 648d6cc).
graft.use_case: NixOS VM tests (Jacquard's `nix flake check`: app-deploy, dashboard, dotfiles-plan, pull-deploy, push-deploy) need KVM and should run locally on vgwsl2 instead of on GitHub's runners. Once Windows exposes AMD-V, vgwsl2 checks /dev/kvm and loads kvm-amd if it's still missing.

answer.text: Nothing on the Windows side is missing: .wslconfig already says nestedVirtualization=true, and it's now declared here (home/wsl/wslconfig, copied by dot apply) so the next machine gets it. VBS / Memory Integrity aren't the cause. vghydra is on 26200.9711 with KB5127648, whose AMD hypervisor (hvax64.exe 10.0.26100.9711) regressed nested virtualization on AMD hosts: same symptoms confirmed here (0 svm, no /dev/kvm, Nested features: 0x0). Microsoft has acknowledged it (microsoft/WSL#41917, 2026-10-19: 'a Windows update is being worked on to restore this functionality'), no date yet. The only workaround is removing the October rollup, which drops its security fixes; that's the user's call. Until then vgwsl2 has no KVM: keep the NixOS VM tests on GitHub's runners. This stays planned: once Microsoft's fix is installed, KVM is checked again here and you'll hear back.
